Source documentation does not establish software or physical hardware qualification. See the support and qualification records for their exact scope.

Typed I/O: devices and execution contracts¶

These declarations come from public header files. Selection, lifecycle, supported execution modes and physical authorization remain bounded by the corresponding design and support records.

The Native model controls in model.h, spi_dma_model.h and rtc_lptim_model.h support host tests. They do not establish MCU hardware support or device discovery. Optional interfaces describe selected contracts; their presence does not imply support on every provider.

nx_result_t nx_adc_port_sample(const nx_adc_port_t *port, uint16_t *samples, size_t capacity, nx_time_us_t deadline, size_t *count)¶

Sample the fixed single/scan sequence by bounded polling.

Note

CPU-active task-only acquisition. Reference voltage, sampling error and maximum rate need physical qualification.

Parameters:

  • port – [inout] Single execution owner; fixed channel/sample-time setup.

  • samples – [out] Raw counts in configured channel order.

  • capacity – [in] Sample capacity at least channel_count.

  • count – [out] Complete valid samples; remaining output is untouched.

Returns:

Success or INVALID/BUSY/TIMEOUT/IO; abort/drain completes before return. No retained buffer, DMA/trigger/stream promise.

nx_result_t nx_adc_port_stream_start(const nx_adc_port_t *port, nx_stream_t *stream, uint32_t trigger_hz)¶

Start selected trigger/block acquisition with caller storage.

Note

Blocks contain native uint16_t raw counts in channel order. Capacities and lengths are multiples of a complete scan; DMA domains/alignment and physical rate require separate evidence.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Trigger/block-capable provider, one task executor.

  • stream – [inout] Initialized immutable-consumer block mechanism.

  • trigger_hz – [in] Positive requested complete-scan rate; provider rejects rates outside its declared timer/ADC capability.

Returns:

Success or INVALID/BUSY/UNSUPPORTED before buffer admission.

nx_result_t nx_adc_port_stream_stop(const nx_adc_port_t *port)¶

Stop trigger and memory sources without revoking consumer loans.

Note

Consumer READY/BORROWED blocks must still be drained/released.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Same acquisition executor; retain storage on BUSY.

Returns:

Success proves source detach, BUSY retains producer storage, UNSUPPORTED for a polling-only provider.

nx_result_t nx_adc_port_stream_service(const nx_adc_port_t *port)¶

Explicitly resume discrete block acquisition after consumer drain.

Note

No task, retry or hidden rearm is created. Block modes state their trigger gaps; continuous zero-gap capture requires a separately declared hardware capability and qualification.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Same single task executor as start and stop.

Returns:

Success when an engine is armed, BUSY during source drain or free-block backpressure, STATE after acquisition stops.

nx_result_t nx_adc_port_attach_wake(const nx_adc_port_t *port, const nx_irq_wake_t *wake, uint8_t syscall_ceiling)¶

nx_result_t nx_adc_format_decode(const nx_adc_format_t *format, const void *samples, size_t bytes, size_t scan, size_t channel, int64_t *value)¶

Decode one integer from a caller-owned or consumer-acquired scan.

Note

No pointer is retained. Input/output/format overlap and wrapping spans reject before access. Sample loads have bounded1..4 byte work. This operation performs neither calibrated engineering-unit conversion nor synchronization with an active producer. The consumer owns that join.

Parameters:

  • format – [in] Valid immutable uniform-channel scan description.

  • samples – [in] Readable storage; any producer/DMA access must be joined.

  • bytes – [in] Positive exact multiple of scan_stride, including padding.

  • scan – [in] Zero-based complete scan index.

  • channel – [in] Zero-based channel position in provider order.

  • value – [out] Separate aligned output, unchanged on rejection.

Returns:

SUCCESS or INVALID; all32-bit unsigned/signed raw values fit int64_t.

struct nx_adc_format_t¶
#include <adc_format.h>

Immutable uniform-channel integer layout, independent of ADC faces.

Note

storage_bytes is1..4; significant_bits is1..32 within that storage. lsb_bits names discarded low bits, not an arithmetic scaling factor. sample_stride and scan_stride include explicit padding in bytes. channel_count retains the provider’s separately declared channel order. Software triggers use identity0; hardware trigger identities are nonzero assembly-local IDs, never addresses or a promise of physical timing. Group/trigger declarations describe an already supported provider mode; validating a layout does not add support to a device or configure it.

nx_result_t nx_adc_group_prepare(nx_adc_group_request_t *request, void *frames, size_t bytes, size_t frame_count, nx_time_us_t deadline)¶

Prepare caller storage without hardware access or retained borrow.

Note

Request and frames are distinct. Preparation reads no sample bytes and does not prove a DMA domain or chip mode. All previous observers must be joined before reuse. NX_DEADLINE_NEVER is rejected.

Parameters:

  • request – [inout] Initialized READY or fully consumed SETTLED storage.

  • frames – [out] Aligned nonempty raw output including explicit padding.

  • bytes – [in] Positive nonwrapping span; provider validates exact layout.

  • frame_count – [in] Positive whole-frame count, not a raw rank count.

  • deadline – [in] Finite absolute deadline in platform monotonic domain.

Returns:

SUCCESS or INVALID/STATE, rejected request remains unchanged.

nx_result_t nx_adc_group_submit(const nx_adc_group_port_t *port, nx_adc_group_request_t *request)¶

Accept and start one selected finite acquisition under a sole owner.

Note

Accepted descriptor is caller-immutable; caller cannot access frames until acquire-observed SETTLED. Priming may write this entire span but never publishes prime data as valid. Post-admission arm failure keeps the borrow until actual drain. Without trusted completion timestamps, completion first observed at/after deadline is TIMEOUT. One-frame injected profiles deliberately prevent a second trigger/JDR overwrite.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Initialized selected face with immutable retained facts.

  • request – [inout] Exact READY descriptor and exclusive writable span.

Returns:

SUCCESS means ACCEPTED, including immediate SETTLED failure. Other results reject without pointer retention or residual new effects.

nx_result_t nx_adc_group_cancel(const nx_adc_group_port_t *port, nx_adc_group_request_t *request)¶

Start cancellation without revoking the accepted storage borrow.

Note

The first terminal fault/cancel/timeout remains authoritative.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Same stable selected face and serialized privileged task.

  • request – [inout] Exact current accepted request, still live.

Returns:

SUCCESS starts/observes cancellation; it does not imply SETTLED.

nx_result_t nx_adc_group_service(const nx_adc_group_port_t *port)¶

Make bounded prime/acquisition/drain progress without hidden waits.

Note

No request or output is reclaimed while sources, ADC, DMA or IRQs may still reference it. QUARANTINED requests remain owned and retryable.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Same stable selected face and serialized privileged task.

Returns:

SUCCESS after progress/settlement, BUSY during outstanding drain, or an error with retained recovery responsibility.

nx_result_t nx_adc_group_stop(const nx_adc_group_port_t *port)¶

Close admission and prove request source drain before reporting idle.

Note

Stop is not cold close: pads, common clock, internal-source enables and provider storage remain retained until platform joined close.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Same stable selected face and serialized privileged task.

Returns:

SUCCESS only after final request detach; BUSY/IO keeps all leases.

nx_result_t nx_adc_group_info(const nx_adc_group_port_t *port, nx_adc_group_info_t *info)¶

Copy actual selected facts and current retained owner state.

Note

Observing idle/fault does not release a request or any cold lease.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Same initialized selected face, unique task executor.

  • info – [out] Separate aligned output, unchanged on rejection.

Returns:

SUCCESS or INVALID/STATE/CONTEXT/UNSUPPORTED.

nx_result_t nx_advanced_pwm_set_duty(const nx_advanced_pwm_t *port, uint32_t duty_ticks)¶

Stage duty against the fixed declared PSC/ARR and complementary pair.

Note

Shadow duty becomes effective at the next update. Hardware deadtime encoding must exactly represent the cold-configured tDTS count; PSC does not scale deadtime. This API does not certify pin timing.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] One serialized privileged task owner.

  • duty_ticks – [in] Zero through the maintained period, inclusive.

Returns:

SUCCESS or INVALID/STATE/CONTEXT; no base-clock reconfiguration.

nx_result_t nx_advanced_pwm_start(const nx_advanced_pwm_t *port)¶

Enable outputs only with inactive break and no latched fault.

Note

Automatic output reenabling and irreversible hardware LOCK are prohibited. A break never silently starts outputs again.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Privileged task owner of reviewed pin/clock/vector leases.

Returns:

SUCCESS or BUSY/STATE/IO/CONTEXT; failure retains ownership.

nx_result_t nx_advanced_pwm_stop(const nx_advanced_pwm_t *port)¶

Disable/read back master output and both channel sources.

Note

Cold assembly keeps the reviewed inactive-pin and shared-vector leases until success and IRQ quiescence. A latched break survives stop.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Privileged task owner, no concurrent duty/lifecycle calls.

Returns:

SUCCESS proves output source detachment; BUSY retains responsibility.

nx_result_t nx_advanced_pwm_state(const nx_advanced_pwm_t *port, nx_advanced_pwm_state_t *state)¶

Query staged duty, actual enable state and latched break facts.

Parameters:

  • state – [out] Separate writable snapshot, never provider storage.

Returns:

SUCCESS or INVALID/STATE/CONTEXT.

nx_result_t nx_advanced_pwm_clear_fault(const nx_advanced_pwm_t *port)¶

Clear a software fault only while disabled and BKIN is inactive.

Note

Physical input and pending hardware break are rechecked. Application recovery policy and external power safety remain outside Nexus.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Privileged task recovery owner.

Returns:

SUCCESS or BUSY/STATE/IO/CONTEXT; does not enable outputs.

nx_result_t nx_can_port_stop(const nx_can_port_t *port)¶

Close admission, abort TX and detach IRQ/RX publishers.

Success after bounded hardware acknowledgement, BUSY while borrowed.

nx_result_t nx_can_port_attach_wake(const nx_can_port_t *port, const nx_irq_wake_t *wake, uint8_t syscall_ceiling)¶

Borrow an optional wake target after checking all four actual IRQs.

Note

No implicit OS policy; NULL detaches. Wake is only a hint. The sink must support both task service/cancel and configurable IRQ contexts.

Returns:

Success, BUSY while an earlier publisher is live, PERMISSION, INVALID or CONTEXT, with no new borrow on failure.

A valid request snapshot has a nonzero epoch and finite observed_at; its deadline may be NX_DEADLINE_NEVER to mean no deadline. SERVICE facts require finite last_service_at and observed_at in the same monotonic domain, and a finite positive maximum_service_gap_us. Unknown groups stay unknown.

struct nx_io_diagnostic_facts_t¶
#include <diagnostic.h>

Stable caller copies, with independently known fact groups.

Note

request/stream may be NULL; their presence establishes the corresponding group. known accepts only LIFECYCLE, OWNER, SERVICE and OBSERVERS. Zero-initialized unknown values never establish readiness, health or a missed service. OWNER fields may come from an owner observer only when its diagnostic_result succeeded. They describe admission and pending work, not the cause of a BUSY service result. SERVICE timestamps use the same monotonic domain; both are finite and maximum_service_gap_us is a finite positive declared budget. This helper reads no clock itself. Copies remain stable throughout this call. Observations need not be simultaneous across devices.

Bounded task/IRQ check, no MMIO, allocation or side effects.

nx_result_t nx_dma_storage_validate(const nx_dma_memory_region_t *regions, size_t count, const void *storage, size_t capacity, size_t transfer_bytes, size_t alignment, size_t cache_line_bytes, nx_dma_direction_t direction)¶

Check an explicit owned reservation and its DMA payload.

Note

Bounded task/IRQ validation, no allocation/cache operation. Callers exclusively own all lines and padding until drain and acquire-observed SETTLED. This validates geometry only; it cannot prove ownership or replace provider admission, actual cache geometry, mode-specific length checks or cache maintenance. Cancellation never releases that obligation.

Parameters:

  • regions – [in] Immutable reviewed SoC DMA domains, not retained.

  • count – [in] Positive domain count.

  • storage – [in] Caller-owned reservation, distinct from live loans.

  • capacity – [in] Whole reservation bytes, including owned padding.

  • transfer_bytes – [in] Positive payload size, at most capacity.

  • alignment – [in] Nonzero power-of-two transfer alignment.

  • cache_line_bytes – [in] Zero for no cache constraint, otherwise a reviewed power-of-two line size; address and capacity must be exact multiples. The helper never rounds ranges.

  • direction – [in] Device access permission for the whole storage.

Returns:

SUCCESS, INVALID or PERMISSION; no memory access or borrow.

entropy.h¶

The entropy face supplies bounded, health-admitted source words. nx_entropy_fill uses a finite absolute deadline and erases the complete admitted output on a read failure. It does not allocate, create a worker or establish entropy quality; it is not a DRBG. A source’s existence does not authorize full entropy credit for a cryptographic library. See the explicit F407 constructor for its clock and shutdown prerequisites. GD32 entropy is not implemented.

Explicit entropy source and finite all-or-erased filling.

Author

Nexus Team

Typedefs

typedef struct nx_entropy_port nx_entropy_port_t¶

Static two-pointer source face with private mutable state.

Note

Caller serializes use and lifecycle; face/table/state outlive each call. No buffer or request is retained after return. Source enable, clock dependencies, recovery and stop belong to its explicit lifecycle owner, not to TLS or this face.

Functions

nx_result_t nx_entropy_port_try_read(const nx_entropy_port_t *port, uint32_t *word)¶

Try to copy one complete source word without waiting.

Note

Invalid public spans reject before provider access. This wrapper cannot infer the extent of an opaque context; the caller proves its complete disjointness. Provider rejection never substitutes fixed values or timestamps for entropy.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Live immutable face on its serialized task executor

  • word – [out] Naturally aligned writable word, disjoint from face, table and the complete private provider state

Returns:

SUCCESS, BUSY, IO, STATE, INVALID or UNSUPPORTED

nx_result_t nx_entropy_fill(const nx_entropy_port_t *port, void *output, size_t bytes, const nx_clock_t *clock, nx_time_us_t deadline)¶

Fill exactly the requested bytes before a finite deadline.

Note

Task-only synchronous polling; no heap, worker or OS wait. BUSY causes another clock-bounded poll. The supplied clock must continue advancing throughout the call; changing its domain or stopping its timer violates the contract. NX_DEADLINE_NEVER is rejected. Complete words are emitted least-significant byte first; unused final-word bytes are discarded. A zero-byte request validates face and clock but performs no clock/source access and accepts NULL output. Preflight rejection leaves output unchanged. Once admitted, any error erases the complete output using volatile writes; no partial entropy may be consumed. Output is disjoint from face/table/clock and all their opaque live contexts. This function detects known-span aliases, not opaque extents. Crypto libraries own conditioning, DRBGs and trust policy.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Live serialized source; no concurrent lifecycle change

  • output – [out] Writable byte span; NULL only for zero bytes

  • bytes – [in] Exact required output size, not an entropy estimate

  • clock – [in] Live monotonic microsecond clock in one stable domain

  • deadline – [in] Finite absolute deadline in that clock domain

Returns:

SUCCESS only for a complete fill; TIMEOUT, IO, STATE or source error; INVALID/UNSUPPORTED for preflight rejection

struct nx_entropy_ops_t¶
#include <entropy.h>

Shared immutable entropy-source methods.

Note

try_read is task-only and bounded, never waits for hardware. SUCCESS copies one complete health-admitted 32-bit word; BUSY means no word yet, IO means a source/health failure, STATE means unavailable/closed. Failure leaves output unchanged. The provider owns hardware health and initial sample handling. No deterministic fallback, conditioning, DRBG or cryptographic certification is implied.

nx_result_t nx_eth_port_apply_link(const nx_eth_port_t *port, const nx_eth_link_t *link)¶

Apply external PHY observations, not auto-negotiate or invent link.

Note

Task owner; changing speed/duplex first requires explicit link-down and observed idle TX/RX engines and FIFOs. BUSY keeps the old mode. Reapplying an unchanged up fact is idempotent. Link-down closes admission and drains pending TX with IO; later up requires real quiescence. This is not a PHY power/reset/electrical proof.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Serialized task-owner face.

  • link – [in] Observed up/speed/duplex fact, never a guess.

Returns:

Success, BUSY until real drain, or STATE/IO/context error.

nx_result_t nx_eth_port_stop(const nx_eth_port_t *port)¶

Close admission and withdraw MAC/DMA/IRQ sources with readback.

Note

Task owner. Closing rejects new RX loans; existing loans still release. BUSY retains hardware/storage/wake ownership; timeout quarantines pending TX. Held RX loans remain valid and must be released before SUCCESS. Caller joins IRQ/consumers before reclaiming storage.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Live face and all storage, including held loans.

Returns:

Success releases sources; BUSY/IO retain remaining ownership.

nx_result_t nx_eth_port_attach_wake(const nx_eth_port_t *port, const nx_irq_wake_t *wake, uint8_t syscall_ceiling)¶

Bind an optional borrowed hint after actual IRQ-policy validation.

Note

Task owner with no pending TX; notify is bounded and legal in IRQ. Service does not invoke the IRQ hint from a task. Detach after stop.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Started serialized task-owner face.

  • wake – [in] Borrowed IRQ hint; NULL requests detach.

  • syscall_ceiling – [in] Exact configured unshifted syscall ceiling.

Returns:

Success, BUSY while publishers live, or policy/context error.

Optional scatter-gather frame and MAC-clock loans.

Author

Nexus Team

Note

Physical qualification is separate from software validation.

Defines

NX_ETH_FRAMES_CAPTURE_CORRUPT¶

Capture diagnostics; UNKNOWN stamp remains unusable measurement.

Functions

nx_result_t nx_eth_frames_tx_prepare(nx_eth_frames_tx_request_t *request, const nx_eth_fragment_t *fragments, size_t fragment_count, bool timestamp, nx_time_us_t deadline)¶

Prepare unborrowed request storage without hardware effects.

Note

Serialized task owner. Validate nonempty fragments, overflow and the complete Ethernet II header across fragments; permit one in-band C-tag. Untagged length is 14..1514, tagged 18..1518, excluding FCS. Hardware inserts padding/FCS. Length-coded 802.3, QinQ and 0x88A8 reject. Failure preserves request and retains no references. Deadline is an absolute monotonic provider time, distinct from the PTP clock domain.

nx_result_t nx_eth_frames_port_submit(const nx_eth_frames_port_t *port, nx_eth_frames_tx_request_t *request)¶

ACCEPT one complete frame after all storage and slots are validated.

Note

Task owner, privileged/unmasked; no pool, heap, worker or OS lock. REJECTED retains no references or OWN effects. ACCEPTED borrows request, fragment array and every payload until acquire-observed SETTLED. One returned descriptor does not prove wire completion. transferred is whole frame bytes on proven MAC success, otherwise zero.

nx_result_t nx_eth_frames_port_cancel(const nx_eth_frames_port_t *port, nx_eth_frames_tx_request_t *request)¶

Request controller-wide TX withdrawal without replay.

Note

Other pending TX are cancelled too; observed completed wire success can win. No cancellation revokes a borrow. Missing drain proof keeps QUARANTINED loans. This does not reset the shared MAC/PTP/RX owner.

nx_result_t nx_eth_frames_port_service(const nx_eth_frames_port_t *port)¶

Bounded task progress; IRQ handles at most one descriptor per side.

nx_result_t nx_eth_frames_port_acquire(const nx_eth_frames_port_t *port, nx_eth_frames_rx_loan_t *loan, nx_eth_fragment_t *fragments, size_t capacity)¶

Acquire one complete frame with whole-frame capacity admission.

Note

One task consumer. EMPTY creates no loan; OVERFLOW for too few views leaves the complete frame queued and all outputs unchanged. Stop closes new acquisitions. Held descriptors are never rearmed at wrap or stop.

nx_result_t nx_eth_frames_port_release(const nx_eth_frames_port_t *port, const nx_eth_frames_rx_loan_t *loan)¶

Final consumer access; stale/altered/foreign/double release rejects.

nx_result_t nx_eth_frames_port_state(const nx_eth_frames_port_t *port, nx_eth_frames_state_t *state)¶

Copy latched facts to unretained output disjoint from every loan.

nx_result_t nx_eth_frames_port_clock(const nx_eth_frames_port_t *port, nx_io_timestamp_t *stamp)¶

Read a coherent current hardware counter in its own domain.

Note

No clock synchronization, UTC mapping, acquired-time fallback or PHY compensation. source is SERVICE_OBSERVATION, not an SFD event. The owner extends seconds wrap and rejects regression, overflow and ambiguous gaps; ticks are nanoseconds with rate1e9 and unknown uncertainty.

nx_result_t nx_eth_frames_port_apply_link(const nx_eth_frames_port_t *port, const nx_eth_link_t *link)¶

Apply explicit external PHY observation after real TX/RX quiet.

nx_result_t nx_eth_frames_port_stop(const nx_eth_frames_port_t *port)¶

Close admission and prove DMA/MAC/IRQ withdrawal before release.

Note

Held RX and captured publishers retain ownership. Any failure keeps unfinished leases. Do not flush a nonempty TX FIFO to fake quiet. Caller joins all external producers/consumers/observers separately.

nx_result_t nx_eth_frames_port_recover(const nx_eth_frames_port_t *port, nx_time_us_t deadline)¶

Explicit recovery by the exclusive MAC owner after failed drain.

Note

Task owner; finite absolute deadline. Held RX or captured publishers return BUSY without reset. Reset acknowledgement is mandatory before detached pending TX can settle with their locked terminal cause; never report wire success without its actual status. No auto replay. Reset invalidates the old hardware clock epoch and records an RX gap. Source failure/timeout retains QUARANTINED loans and recovery responsibility.

nx_result_t nx_eth_frames_port_attach_wake(const nx_eth_frames_port_t *port, const nx_irq_wake_t *wake, uint8_t syscall_ceiling)¶

Optional borrowed IRQ hint; validate actual priority, detach/join.

nx_result_t nx_flash_port_program(const nx_flash_port_t *port, uint32_t offset, const void *data, size_t length, nx_time_us_t deadline)¶

Program aligned physical Flash and settle all hardware pulses.

Note

Task-only CPU-active operation. Product owns execution-from- Flash stall, watchdog and power-loss policy. No RAM fake on MCU.

Note

With NX_FLASH_PROGRAM_REQUIRES_FRESH_ERASE, each programmed unit needs a successful erase and no later program pulse. Reading all 0xff cannot prove this on ECC Flash. A failed or interrupted pulse consumes its unit until the next successful sector erase. The caller owns this provenance; providers keep no implicit erase-history bitmap.

Note

All-0xff input units must not issue a program pulse. A provider may reject a visibly non-erased destination.

Parameters:

  • port – [inout] Single execution owner with valid voltage/clock policy.

  • offset – [in] Program-unit aligned physical offset.

  • data – [in] Aligned-length input retained only until return.

  • length – [in] Positive program-unit multiple.

  • deadline – [in] Absolute deadline checked between hardware pulses.

Returns:

Success or INVALID/TIMEOUT/IO. Return proves no remaining buffer/hardware access; an active pulse cannot be preempted.

nx_result_t nx_flash_port_erase(const nx_flash_port_t *port, uint32_t offset, size_t length, nx_time_us_t deadline)¶

Erase a whole physical sector range with pulse settlement.

Parameters:

  • port – [inout] Single execution owner.

  • offset – [in] Exact sector-start physical offset.

  • length – [in] Positive sum of whole sectors.

  • deadline – [in] Absolute deadline checked between erase pulses.

Returns:

Success or INVALID/TIMEOUT/IO; partial erase is possible on timeout/error. Return waits for current pulse to become idle.

i2c_bus_clear.h¶

Explicit open-drain I2C bus clear with retained leases.

Author

Nexus Team

Defines

NX_I2C_BUS_CLEAR_MAX_PULSES¶

Maximum completed recovery low/high periods per attempt.

Functions

nx_result_t nx_i2c_bus_clear_init(nx_i2c_bus_clear_t *clear, nx_i2c_bus_clear_port_t port, nx_clock_t clock, nx_i2c_bus_clear_timing_t timing)¶

Bind explicit electrical operations without touching pins.

Parameters:

  • clear – [inout] Fresh zeroed session or a session with no lease.

  • port – [in] All five methods required; caller verifies electrical authorization rather than relying on generic GPIO APIs.

  • clock – [in] Required bounded monotonic read in one boot domain.

  • timing – [in] Reviewed nonzero low/high/STOP/poll durations.

Returns:

SUCCESS, INVALID or BUSY for a retained lease. Rejection leaves the session and external resources unchanged.

nx_result_t nx_i2c_bus_clear_run(nx_i2c_bus_clear_t *clear, nx_time_us_t deadline, nx_time_us_t cleanup_deadline, nx_i2c_bus_clear_result_t *result)¶

Clear one idle, authorized bus with at most nine pulses.

Note

Task-only, all other bus users quiescent. Timing evidence and actual open-drain behavior require physical HIL.

Parameters:

  • clear – [inout] Initialized session with no retained lease.

  • deadline – [in] Finite absolute primary-operation deadline.

  • cleanup_deadline – [in] Finite absolute STOP/lease deadline in the same clock domain, at or after deadline.

  • result – [out] Independent primary/cleanup and retained effects.

Returns:

Primary failure, otherwise cleanup result. Invalid inputs and an existing lease reject without callbacks or changing result. An expired primary deadline has no pin effects. Each released SCL must be physically HIGH before timing its high period. A frozen/reversed clock reports IO and exits rather than spinning. Every acquired attempt performs explicit STOP cleanup under its independent budget; failed STOP or release method retains the lease. If release succeeds after its deadline, cleanup reports TIMEOUT with lease_held false to preserve actual returned ownership. It never replays the failed I2C transaction or retries recovery pulses.

nx_result_t nx_i2c_bus_clear_finish(nx_i2c_bus_clear_t *clear, nx_time_us_t deadline, nx_i2c_bus_clear_result_t *result)¶

Retry only retained STOP cleanup and ownership return.

Parameters:

  • clear – [inout] Initialized session with a retained lease.

  • deadline – [in] New finite absolute cleanup deadline.

  • result – [out] Preserved primary/pulse count and latest cleanup.

Returns:

Latest cleanup result; INVALID/STATE rejects without effects. A proved STOP is not repeated after release fails. Failure retains the lease and must not trigger a new clear or transaction. Success does not change a failed primary operation into success.

struct nx_i2c_bus_clear_ops_t¶
#include <i2c_bus_clear.h>

Read-only methods for an authorized two-pin GPIO handoff.

Note

Task-only, one executor. acquire is a bounded, nonblocking handoff: success proves the controller, DMA, IRQs, other masters and pin users quiescent, both physical pins exclusively leased in reviewed open-drain GPIO mode, with both lines released. Failure retains no lease or effects. drive only sinks LOW or releases a pin; false never means drive HIGH. When scl_low is true, drive establishes SCL LOW before changing SDA, including a retry from unknown previous pin state. sample reads physical levels, not output latches. Methods are bounded and preserve the lease on errors. release restores the saved peripheral/pin ownership only on success; failure retains all lease/storage responsibility. wait_until uses the injected clock’s finite absolute domain and reaches target or reports an error within a caller- proved finite bound, even if the clock stops. Late waits cannot qualify an expired operation. No callback may recursively operate on this session or run a transaction. The adapter must verify reviewed open-drain, pull-up, voltage and two-pin authorization facts before acquire.

Public Members

nx_result_t (*sample)(void *context, bool *scl_high, bool *sda_high)¶

Owner and nonwrapping shot incarnation, never an RTC/Core token.

Note

Identity is compared without dereference. Tokens/observers must be retired before the owner storage lifetime ends or its address is reused.

struct nx_lptim_sample_t¶
#include <lptim.h>

Declared units and modulo counter, not an absolute time estimate.

Note

A complete 65536-tick shot wraps counter to zero. Counter zero alone cannot establish completion, idle, missed wraps or low-power continuity. tick_hz is a fixed declared rate, not physical oscillator accuracy.

struct nx_lptim_request_t¶
#include <lptim.h>

One caller-owned finite shot; transferred is final observed ticks.

Note

Initialize base first. After ACCEPTED keep the entire request live and caller immutable until acquire-observed SETTLED and external joins. A latched CANCELLED/TIMEOUT fixes the cause, not the final progress: held withdrawal may allow further source ticks before detachment.

mdio.h¶

Narrow Clause22 station management with absolute deadlines.

Author

Nexus Team

Functions

nx_result_t nx_mdio_read(const nx_mdio_port_t *port, uint8_t address, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *value, nx_time_us_t deadline)¶

Read one Clause22 PHY register without retaining output storage.

Note

Serialized privileged task, incoming masks clear; finite absolute deadline in the provider clock. Address and register are 0..31. BUSY rejects before new MMIO effects; timeout does not pretend busy cleared.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Stable face and caller-owned execution context.

  • address – [in] Clause22 PHY address, from 0 through 31.

  • reg – [in] Clause22 register address, from 0 through 31.

  • value – [out] Written only after timely observed completion.

  • deadline – [in] Finite absolute provider-clock deadline.

Returns:

Success, BUSY without a new command, or timeout/input/context error.

nx_result_t nx_mdio_write(const nx_mdio_port_t *port, uint8_t address, uint8_t reg, uint16_t value, nx_time_us_t deadline)¶

Write one Clause22 PHY register, not a PHY-specific policy sequence.

Note

Same task/deadline rules as read. No IRQ-masked busy wait or fallback.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Stable face and caller-owned execution context.

  • address – [in] Clause22 PHY address, from 0 through 31.

  • reg – [in] Clause22 register address, from 0 through 31.

  • value – [in] Exact 16-bit register value.

  • deadline – [in] Finite absolute provider-clock deadline.

Returns:

Success, BUSY without a new command, or timeout/input/context error.

nx_result_t nx_io_timestamp_elapsed(const nx_io_timestamp_t *first, const nx_io_timestamp_t *last, nx_io_timestamp_delta_t *out)¶

Compare two explicitly related observed events.

Note

Task/IRQ pure constant work; no clock, hardware, allocation, lock or reference retention. Inputs may coincide. The caller proves event pairing and timestamp provenance. Different explicit source kinds may be compared to observe delivery latency, without relabeling either observation.

Parameters:

  • first – [in] Stable aligned first fact, not concurrently modified.

  • last – [in] Stable last fact in the same domain, epoch and rate.

  • out – [out] Distinct aligned result, unchanged on rejection.

Returns:

SUCCESS, INVALID for malformed/overlapping storage, UNSUPPORTED for UNKNOWN source, STATE for incompatible domains or reversed ticks, EXHAUSTED for bound overflow.

nx_result_t nx_io_timestamp_budget(const nx_io_timestamp_t *first, const nx_io_timestamp_t *last, uint64_t maximum_ticks, nx_io_timestamp_budget_result_t *out)¶

Compare a complete timing-error interval with a budget.

Note

Pure O(1) Task/IRQ work with no clock access or retention. WITHIN requires upper <= maximum; EXCEEDED requires lower > maximum. An overlapping or unknown error interval gives UNKNOWN. SUCCESS alone does not mean within budget. The existing timestamp-owner/provenance contract applies: this does not extend raw DWT, validate epoch continuity, synchronize sampling, establish IRQ arrival or prove WCET.

Parameters:

  • first – [in] Stable aligned extended timestamp, causally paired.

  • last – [in] Stable aligned fact in the same domain/epoch/rate.

  • maximum_ticks – [in] Inclusive maximum, in the stated tick units.

  • out – [out] Distinct aligned result, unchanged on rejection.

Returns:

SUCCESS, INVALID/UNSUPPORTED/STATE as elapsed, or EXHAUSTED when the uncertainty sum or upper bound cannot fit.

struct nx_io_timestamp_t¶
#include <observation.h>

Explicit, caller-supplied time fact without clock access.

Note

ticks is extended, monotonically increasing within one nonzero domain/epoch. Its owner extends counter wrap and changes epoch on reset, discontinuity or rate change. Domain and epoch are assembly-local identities, not clocks synchronized across cores, security domains or devices. UNKNOWN carries no usable measurement. Frequency is exact stated ticks/second, not measured accuracy. A known zero uncertainty states zero error; unknown uncertainty has a separate flag. These facts do not establish physical precision, causal pairing or event identity by themselves.

pwm_adc.h¶

Optional finite coherent PWM / triggered ADC window.

Author

Nexus Team

Functions

nx_result_t nx_pwm_adc_prepare(nx_pwm_adc_request_t *request, uint16_t *samples, size_t sample_count, const nx_pwm_group_frame_t *frame, nx_time_us_t deadline)¶

Prepare distinct unborrowed request, frame and sample storage.

Note

Request, sample span, source frame descriptor and duty span must be naturally aligned, nonwrapping and disjoint. The caller has consumed prior results and joined every adapter observer before preparing again. NX_DEADLINE_NEVER is rejected; an expired finite deadline can be prepared but cannot admit new physical effects. Preparation does not access sample contents, borrow hardware or establish rate/region support. Failure leaves the initialized request unchanged.

Parameters:

  • request – [inout] Initialized READY or fully consumed SETTLED storage.

  • samples – [out] Naturally aligned writable caller sample array.

  • sample_count – [in] Positive exact sample count; provider checks DMA.

  • frame – [in] Readable descriptor copied by value during this call only; its complete duty array remains live through SETTLED.

  • deadline – [in] Finite absolute monotonic deadline for the whole window.

Returns:

SUCCESS or INVALID/STATE; no hardware access or provider borrow.

nx_result_t nx_pwm_adc_submit(const nx_pwm_adc_t *port, nx_pwm_adc_request_t *request)¶

Admit and arm one complete finite window on the unique task owner.

Note

Post-admission arm/prime failures drain under the accepted request. Normal completion stops the PWM sources before SETTLED and never rearms. DMA TC alone is insufficient for completion or safe output. An error/cancellation reports zero guaranteed valid samples; an aborted DMA remaining count cannot establish a valid prefix. A successful window reports exactly sample_count. After successful ordinary completion, another explicitly prepared submission may begin; an explicit stop or latched fault requires cold close/reinitialization. Provider checks context, fixed frame, region and overlap with all cold descriptors/MMIO before admission. The complete duty frame is constant for the window; sample count does not promise an exact PWM pulse count. Without a trusted completion timestamp, completion first observed at or after the request deadline reports TIMEOUT, even if DMA is already complete. This conservative observation rule promises no physical execution-time bound and never relaxes the required source drain.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Initialized stable selected coupled face and cold leases.

  • request – [inout] Exact READY window prepared by the caller.

Returns:

SUCCESS means ACCEPTED, including a possibly already SETTLED error. Rejection means no retained pointer, payload access or new effect.

nx_result_t nx_pwm_adc_cancel(const nx_pwm_adc_t *port, nx_pwm_adc_request_t *request)¶

Latch cancellation while retaining the exact live window loan.

Note

Cancellation is task-local and does not provide a cross-task stable identity. Use the established adapter slot/epoch mechanism externally. A prior terminal fault is retained; cancellation never clears it.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Same live coupled face and serialized privileged task.

  • request – [inout] Exact admitted request, still live until SETTLED.

Returns:

SUCCESS starts/observes cancellation, never implies SETTLED.

nx_result_t nx_pwm_adc_service(const nx_pwm_adc_t *port)¶

Advance bounded completion or source drain on the same task owner.

Note

No hidden worker/wait/allocation. Only observed source/vector withdrawal permits final pointer detach and release publication.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Same live coupled face and serialized privileged task.

Returns:

SUCCESS after progress/settlement, BUSY while drain remains, or a fault requiring continued recovery service and explicit stop.

nx_result_t nx_pwm_adc_stop(const nx_pwm_adc_t *port)¶

Close admission and attempt final drain without revoking a loan.

Note

Continue the unique service/stop until quiet. Cold close additionally joins vectors and restores saved leases. Fault recovery does not automatically restart PWM or resume acquisition. SUCCESS does not release pads, clocks or private storage. Those cold leases remain held until the platform’s final joined close succeeds.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Same live coupled face and serialized privileged task.

Returns:

SUCCESS proves stopped sources; BUSY/IO retains recovery storage.

nx_result_t nx_pwm_adc_state(const nx_pwm_adc_t *port, nx_pwm_adc_state_t *state)¶

Copy exact fixed facts and observed active/fault/quarantine state.

Note

State is an observation, not a source-drain or release operation.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Same live coupled face and serialized privileged task.

  • state – [out] Distinct aligned output, unchanged on rejection.

Returns:

SUCCESS, INVALID/STATE/CONTEXT or UNSUPPORTED for a missing method.

struct nx_pwm_adc_request_t¶
#include <pwm_adc.h>

One finite window; transferred counts are raw samples, never bytes.

Note

Initialize base before first preparation. After successful admission, the request and duty array remain live and caller-immutable through acquire-observed SETTLED. The writable sample span belongs exclusively to the provider; the caller neither reads nor writes it while borrowed. Frame metadata is copied at preparation. No later shadow commit, automatic rearm, control algorithm or engineering-unit conversion is part of this finite-window interface. Hardware-specific sample storage and integer encoding are reported by state.format.

Borrow and arm one future alarm; no queue, allocation or worker.

Closed/stale/already-matching pattern returns STATE; active is BUSY. An observed expired finite deadline returns TIMEOUT before admission. Calendar, counter and Core deadline are separate domains. Assembly keeps the copied clock face’s borrowed context live, disjoint and non-reentrant for the entire owner lifetime and all external joins.

Parameters:

nx_result_t nx_rtc_port_cancel(const nx_rtc_port_t *port, nx_rtc_request_t *request)¶

Latch cancellation of the exact borrowed request, without revocation.

  • request – [inout] Exact active identity; foreign identity is not read.

nx_result_t nx_rtc_port_service(const nx_rtc_port_t *port)¶

Observe deadline/event or continue actual source withdrawal.

Note

At first observation expiry wins over pending event. Source/pending references detach before release SETTLED, the final provider access.

Parameters:

Returns:

SUCCESS when idle/settled, BUSY while active or withdrawal is held; INVALID/STATE/UNSUPPORTED may reject dispatch.

nx_result_t nx_rtc_port_stop(const nx_rtc_port_t *port)¶

Close admission and prove withdrawal before returning any loan.

Note

Clean repeated stop is idempotent. Stop does not reset identity or revoke pointers. Source/provider lifetime still covers external joins.

Parameters:

Returns:

SUCCESS when closed/joined; BUSY retains the quarantined request. INVALID/STATE/UNSUPPORTED may reject dispatch.

struct nx_rtc_calendar_t¶
#include <rtc.h>

Raw YY calendar; no UTC, century, timezone or oscillator policy.

Note

YY is 00..99 and leap years satisfy YY modulo 4 == 0. Weekday is an independent 1..7 value, not inferred from the date. Other fields use month/day 1-based and 24-hour hour/minute/second values, without leap seconds. Natural year99->00 wrap does not reset the setting domain.

Fixed directions require one byte, other directions length bytes, within reviewed DMA domains. The actual spans must not overlap. Request preparation does not retain these flags; only this successful admission selects them. Ordinary submit and the existing owner continue their ordinary buffer contract.

nx_result_t nx_spi_transaction_validate(const nx_spi_segment_t *segments, size_t count, uint8_t word_bits)¶

Validate every descriptor and span without hardware effects.

Note

No memory is borrowed, copied, allocated or modified. NULL data pointers are legal dummy/discard operations. This does not validate provider-specific controller, rate or limits.

Parameters:

  • segments – [in] Aligned immutable array, retained by the caller.

  • count – [in] Positive descriptor count, at most MAX_SEGMENTS.

nx_result_t nx_spi_transaction_transfer(const nx_spi_transaction_endpoint_t *endpoint, const nx_spi_segment_t *segments, size_t count, uint8_t word_bits, nx_time_us_t deadline, size_t *transferred)¶

Execute all segments under exactly one asserted CS interval.

Note

Task-only single executor; polling is CPU-active. Return releases descriptor/payload borrows after wire drain or provider reset and CS release. Deadline cannot preempt an in-flight word. Errors never replay prior segments. No allocation, OS lock, hidden scratch, width changes or CS toggles occur between phases. This is synchronous: existing finite DMA request and cancellation contracts are unchanged.

Parameters:

  • endpoint – [in] Optional enhanced face with stable private state.

  • segments – [in] Caller-owned descriptors and their data spans.

  • count – [in] Number of phases, all validated before hardware use.

  • word_bits – [in] Common hardware frame width, 8 or 16 bits.

  • deadline – [in] Absolute monotonic deadline for all phases.

  • transferred – [out] Complete received words, never bytes; separate writable size_t storage, reset before provider execution.

Returns:

SUCCESS or INVALID/UNSUPPORTED/CONTEXT/STATE/BUSY/TIMEOUT/IO.

struct nx_spi_segment_t¶
#include <spi_transaction.h>

One phase within a single CS interval.

Note

Words have the transaction’s common width of 8 or 16 bits. NULL TX repeats dummy; NULL RX discards. Both may be NULL for clock-only words. Non-NULL spans contain words elements; 16-bit spans are uint16_t-aligned. Descriptor and TX storage stay immutable until return. RX never overlaps descriptors, TX storage, other RX spans or the completion output. Ordinary byte-span SPI remains a separate unchanged interface.

nx_result_t nx_stream_observe(const nx_stream_t *stream, nx_stream_observation_t *out)¶

Snapshot maintained metadata under one short IRQ guard.

Note

Task/IRQ fixed work, no slot scan or payload access. Caller keeps all storage alive; no observer reference is retained. next_free is the ordinary stream cursor, not the private preposted cursor. Output is distinct from every payload.

Parameters:

  • stream – [in] Live initialized storage, no concurrent destruction.

  • out – [out] Distinct output, unchanged on rejected metadata/alias.

Returns:

nx_result_t nx_stream_budget_calculate(const nx_stream_budget_t *budget, nx_stream_budget_result_t *out)¶

Checked cold calculation, no stream mutation or allocation.

Note

required = targets + spares + ceil(rate*release_delay / (block_units*1000000)); payload is required*block*unit_bytes. Finite math is conservative under the declared FIFO frontier release bound; out-of-order release may still block the next cursor. Latency requires target_delay_us < floor(units_per_block*1000000/units_per_second). This creates no backpressure or hardware qualification.

Parameters:

  • budget – [in] Explicit rate, longest release delay and pipeline.

  • out – [out] Distinct output, unchanged on error or overflow.

Returns:

SUCCESS, INVALID or EXHAUSTED for arithmetic overflow.

stream_profile.h¶

Optional readonly continuous-stream cold admission profiles.

Author

Nexus Team

Functions

nx_result_t nx_uart_stream_profile_start(const nx_uart_stream_profile_t *profile, nx_stream_t *stream)¶

Validate an actual pool before the bound UART may borrow it.

Note

Caller joins all pool users before this cold pool check. Failure before provider dispatch creates no borrow, epoch change or hardware effect. Rate, FIFO-frontier hold and IRQ latency remain declared assumptions, never measurements. This creates no external UART flow control or losslessness. Underlying unprofiled APIs retain their explicit contracts.

Parameters:

  • profile – [in] Stable readonly reviewed binding and assumptions.

  • stream – [inout] Initialized unborrowed pool with exact declared count and equal declared byte capacities, kept live through the original provider’s stop and all consumer releases.

Returns:

INVALID for mismatched geometry/alias, STATE for stopping metadata, BUSY for existing loans, CONTEXT outside an unmasked task, EXHAUSTED for overflow/insufficient budget, UNSUPPORTED for target latency; otherwise provider result.

nx_result_t nx_adc_stream_profile_start(const nx_adc_stream_profile_t *profile, nx_stream_t *stream, uint32_t trigger_hz)¶

Validate pool and whole-scan rate before ADC admission.

Note

ADC stopping its trigger creates a sampling gap. No budget makes that pause preserve wall-clock samples or prove the future consumer/IRQ bounds. No observer/queue is created.

Parameters:

  • profile – [in] Stable readonly binding to the selected ADC face.

  • stream – [inout] Initialized unborrowed exact pool, as for UART.

  • trigger_hz – [in] Positive nominal complete scans per second, no greater than the declared production-rate upper bound.

Returns:

Cold-check errors as for UART, or the original info/start result. Provider scan, timer, DMA/cache and alias checks still apply; no rejected operation retains new references.

struct nx_uart_stream_profile_t¶
#include <stream_profile.h>

Selected UART face and immutable byte-stream assumptions.

Note

Reviewed assembly binds the actual continuous provider. Two hardware targets and one replacement are required. A profile never allocates or owns the caller’s pool. The normal byte face and provider state retain their layouts. Cold admission rechecks payload disjointness in O(n^2); no additional check enters the IRQ or steady I/O path.

nx_result_t nx_timer_capture_start(const nx_timer_capture_t *port, nx_timer_capture_event_t *events, size_t capacity)¶

Borrow an exact event ring and enable the fixed capture channel.

Note

Ring remains borrowed until successful stop. ISR access is confined to this ring. Caller must not modify it or its provider while borrowed. Counter wrap is modulo the reported width; observation time is not an absolute edge timestamp or a clock accuracy qualification.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] One privileged task owner, serialized with stop/read.

  • events – [inout] Aligned writable ring, capacity positive.

  • capacity – [in] Number of events; no hidden buffer or worker.

Returns:

SUCCESS transfers the ring borrow; rejection retains nothing.

nx_result_t nx_timer_capture_stop(const nx_timer_capture_t *port)¶

Disable and read back channel/IRQ sources before returning storage.

Note

Read drains events after capture stops. Failed detach never frees storage. Board pins, timer clock and shared vector leases are released by cold assembly only after successful stop and publisher quiescence.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Privileged task owner, with generated IRQ owner retained.

Returns:

SUCCESS is the final access to the ring; BUSY retains the borrow while queued events or failed hardware detachment remain.

Copy the oldest event in a short saved-mask metadata section.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Single privileged task consumer.

  • event – [out] Separate writable output, unchanged on EMPTY/rejection.

Returns:

SUCCESS, EMPTY, STATE or INVALID; no block release is required.

nx_result_t nx_timer_capture_state(const nx_timer_capture_t *port, nx_timer_capture_state_t *state)¶

Query counter units and observable queue/loss facts.

Note

Hardware overcapture and ring saturation can coalesce edges. A loss incident does not estimate edges, edge frequency or actual IRQ WCET.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Privileged task owner; no concurrent lifecycle writer.

  • state – [out] Separate writable snapshot.

Returns:

SUCCESS or INVALID/STATE/CONTEXT.

nx_result_t nx_uart_tx_prepare(nx_uart_tx_request_t *request, const uint8_t *data, size_t length, nx_time_us_t deadline)¶

Prepare an unborrowed IRQ TX descriptor without copying data.

Parameters:

  • request – [inout] Fresh initialized or consumed SETTLED request.

  • data – [in] Nonempty payload retained unchanged through SETTLED.

  • length – [in] Positive byte count.

  • deadline – [in] Absolute deadline in nx_time_now_us clock domain.

Returns:

NX_SUCCESS or INVALID/STATE; failure retains no buffer.

nx_result_t nx_uart_port_submit(const nx_uart_port_t *port, nx_uart_tx_request_t *request)¶

Submit one direct request to a single-executor UART.

Note

Task-only, bounded admission. TX completion waits for true TC (wire idle). IRQ only moves bytes/publishes hardware facts; the owner calls service to observe deadlines and settle. The first observed terminal fact latches its result. Later service, deadline or cancellation does not overwrite an already observed TC. IRQ/service latency bounds remain provider and product qualification inputs.

Parameters:

  • port – [inout] Initialized idle port owned by this execution context.

  • request – [inout] READY descriptor; borrowed only on NX_SUCCESS.

Returns:

NX_SUCCESS means ACCEPTED, including a later start failure. BUSY/INVALID/CONTEXT/STATE/TIMEOUT means REJECTED with zero borrow; an already expired direct request is not admitted.

nx_result_t nx_uart_port_start_admitted(const nx_uart_port_t *port, nx_uart_tx_request_t *request)¶

Start an adapter-admitted QUEUED request without readmission.

Parameters:

  • port – [inout] Single-executor initialized port.

  • request – [inout] QUEUED descriptor already borrowed by adapter.

Returns:

BUSY retains QUEUED; NX_SUCCESS transfers execution to port. Other start errors must be settled by the adapter executor.

nx_result_t nx_uart_port_cancel(const nx_uart_port_t *port, nx_uart_tx_request_t *request)¶

Request cancellation; acceptance does not mean settlement.

Parameters:

  • port – [inout] Same single execution owner as submit/service.

  • request – [inout] Active live descriptor; cross-task callers use a stable adapter slot and expected epoch instead of this pointer.

Returns:

NX_SUCCESS for pending/already settled cancellation; STATE for a different request. Borrow continues until SETTLED.

void nx_uart_port_service(const nx_uart_port_t *port)¶

Observe time/hardware completion and drain one active request.

Note

Bounded, no wait/callback; call throughout stop/drain and at the declared maximum service interval. Publication is final request access. Hardware unable to drain retains QUARANTINED.

Parameters:

  • port – [inout] Single task/loop execution owner.

nx_result_t nx_uart_port_read_events(const nx_uart_port_t *port, nx_uart_rx_event_t *events, size_t capacity, size_t *count)¶

Read buffered RX events from the selected event profile.

Parameters:

  • port – [inout] Initialized event-profile port; one consumer.

  • events – [out] Caller-owned destination; not retained.

  • capacity – [in] Destination event count.

  • count – [out] Events copied, including explicit loss/error flags.

Returns:

NX_SUCCESS, EMPTY or INVALID/UNSUPPORTED. IRQ produces only into configured storage; overflow never silently overwrites.

nx_result_t nx_uart_port_read_bytes(const nx_uart_port_t *port, uint8_t *bytes, size_t capacity, size_t *count)¶

Read buffered bytes from the selected byte profile.

Parameters:

  • port – [inout] Initialized byte-profile port; one consumer.

  • bytes – [out] Caller-owned destination; not retained.

  • capacity – [in] Destination capacity in bytes.

  • count – [out] Bytes copied; valid on OVERFLOW and on a provider IO failure after copying bytes and attempting RX rearm.

Returns:

NX_SUCCESS, EMPTY, OVERFLOW or INVALID/UNSUPPORTED. Byte profile reports aggregate loss without invented timestamps. A provider can return IO if RX source rearm fails after copying; count and copied bytes remain valid. Admission closes and retained hardware requires verified stop.

nx_result_t nx_uart_port_stop(const nx_uart_port_t *port)¶

Close admission and drain TX before releasing hardware.

Note

RX/IRQ and external consumers must quiesce before storage reclamation. No automatic task/notification destruction.

Parameters:

  • port – [inout] Owner; producers must already have quiesced.

Returns:

NX_SUCCESS when stopped; BUSY while service must continue.

nx_result_t nx_uart_port_attach_wake(const nx_uart_port_t *port, const nx_irq_wake_t *wake, uint8_t syscall_ceiling)¶

Attach or detach one explicit IRQ wake target.

Note

Quiesce every previous publisher before reclaiming an old target. IRQ events latch RX/completion facts before notifying. Detachment removes future publications; notification storage still requires joining external waiters and callbacks.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Initialized provider, controlled by one task executor.

  • wake – [in] Immutable live target or NULL to detach.

  • syscall_ceiling – [in] Optional additional unshifted kernel-safe priority floor; cannot weaken generated policy. PRIMASK kernel targets require zero. Ignored without kernel calls.

Returns:

Success, CONTEXT outside task control, PERMISSION for unsafe actual IRQ priority, or provider STATE/UNSUPPORTED.

nx_result_t nx_uart_port_rx_start(const nx_uart_port_t *port, nx_stream_t *stream)¶

Start the selected RX block mode using exact caller storage.

Note

Provider boundaries and gaps are explicit capability facts. The provider must never overwrite a borrowed consumer block.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Block-capable provider, one task execution owner.

  • stream – [inout] Initialized block stream retained until RX stops and all acquired consumer blocks are released.

Returns:

Success or INVALID/BUSY/UNSUPPORTED with zero failed admission loan; selected hardware modes validate every DMA block domain.

nx_result_t nx_uart_port_rx_stop(const nx_uart_port_t *port)¶

Stop RX block production without revoking consumer loans.

Note

Consumers separately drain READY blocks and release loans; successful RX stop does not destroy stream or wake storage.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Same executor as RX start; storage stays live on BUSY.

Returns:

Success proves memory sources detached; BUSY retains producer loan, UNSUPPORTED for a byte/event-only provider.

struct nx_uart_rx_event_t¶
#include <uart.h>

Timestamp belongs to provider clock; precision is hardware-specific.

Note

NO_BYTE marks status-only IRQ facts: byte is invalid. LOSS is an independent NO_BYTE boundary marker, ordered after older buffered facts and before later reception. Its timestamp is provider detection/report time, never a reconstructed timestamp for missing bytes. Byte-profile reads report aggregate loss and omit status-only facts.

Bind exclusive transport and establish inactive DE.

Note

Task-only, no wait. No physical transceiver is inferred. Setup starts after successful DE assertion; hold starts after acquire-observed true transport settlement. Transfer deadline includes setup and wire completion; mandatory drain/hold may extend the borrow beyond that deadline. Rejected TX leaves DE and transport unchanged. Failed drain or DE withdrawal keeps QUARANTINED outer storage and DE ownership until service retry.

  • config – [in] Immutable lifetime binding; one authorized DE bit, real board polarity, setup/hold in nx_time_now_us domain.

Explicitly activate or deactivate one selected nonzero direction.

Note

No request or buffer is borrowed. Existing loans must be explicitly cancelled and drained before target changes; failure never revokes other loans. Configuration/class policy remains external.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Started serialized privileged Task owner, IRQ masks clear.

  • epoch – [in] Current software USB epoch; cold epoch zero is valid.

  • endpoint_address – [in] USB address byte; EP0 is not admitted.

  • active – [in] Requested active state, never packet submission.

Returns:

Success after proof; UNSUPPORTED when the operation is absent. INVALID/CONTEXT/STATE/BUSY reject before writes. IO may have partial effects and closes controller admission until explicit recovery.

Admit one packet, never a hidden queue or complete USB transaction.

One privileged task executor, IRQ masks clear. IN FIFO writes do not prove host ACK. OUT overrun drains all packet words without overflow.

Request endpoint disable/drain without revoking a buffer loan.

Note

Control OUT0 has no hardware disable command: cancellation may require full device stop to settle. Missing proof becomes QUARANTINED. Reset/SETUP invalidates epochs but releases only after actual source drain.

  • request – [inout] Live request accepted by this exact endpoint.

Returns:

Success requests drain; failures retain all prior accepted loans.

nx_result_t nx_usb_device_stop(const nx_usb_device_port_t *port)¶

Disconnect, disable, drain, detach IRQs, then release clock consumer.

Note

PIO OUT0 may remain enabled: successful global stop proves disconnect, OUT NAK, no DMA, empty RX FIFO, IRQ withdrawal and publisher join before final SETTLED. No forced reset revokes an unproved accepted borrow.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Serialized owner; external observers must also join.

Returns:

Success ends provider access to endpoint/ring/wake storage; BUSY retains all storage and 48MHz ownership until actual progress.

nx_result_t nx_usb_profile_validate(const nx_usb_device_profile_t *profile)¶

Validate exact selected FS facts without observing the controller.

Note

Task/ISR bounded and read-only. Facts identify selected software support; they never imply PCB routing, VBUS wiring or physical qualification. Public metadata, endpoint arrays, faces and operations tables require their natural C alignment and nonwrapping extents. Numeric rejection is not a probe of arbitrary addresses or opaque private contexts. EP0 selects control/64; nonzero bulk selects 8/16/32/64-byte MPS. Interrupt selects nonzero IN with 1..64-byte MPS. Host polling interval belongs to the external descriptor, not this profile.

Parameters:

  • profile – [in] Stable readable immutable facts, faces and endpoint array.

Returns:

Success or INVALID, including misaligned public metadata; no allocation, MMIO, discovery or lifecycle effect.

const nx_usb_endpoint_profile_t *nx_usb_profile_endpoint(const nx_usb_device_profile_t *profile, uint8_t number, bool in)¶

Find a direction in a previously validated immutable profile.

Note

Task/ISR read-only bounded lookup; all input lifetimes remain external.

Parameters:

  • profile – [in] Stable validated selected facts and endpoint array.

  • number – [in] Endpoint number, independent of direction.

  • in – [in] IN direction when true; OUT when false.

Returns:

Selected stable member or NULL, including misaligned profile/array metadata. No new endpoint can be discovered.

nx_result_t nx_usb_setup_reject(const nx_usb_setup_decision_port_t *port, uint64_t epoch)¶

Reject one published SETUP epoch by a checked EP0 IN STALL.

Note

Same privileged unmasked single task executor. The provider checks its published epoch and performs STALL in one local IRQ critical section, preserving the incoming mask. This excludes an already software-published replacement SETUP; it does not promise atomicity with physical bus packets not yet collected by the IRQ. No cancellation, global stop, allocation, class policy or address commit is implicit.

Parameters:

  • port – [in] Stable selected decision face, same controller owner.

  • epoch – [in] Nonzero software-published SETUP identity to reject.

Returns:

Success after guarded STALL readback; STATE for a superseded epoch/closing source, BUSY while either EP0 packet is live, INVALID for malformed metadata, CONTEXT for an invalid executor, IO for failed STALL readback, or UNSUPPORTED without the optional operation. Rejection retains no loan.

nx_result_t nx_irq_wake_validate(const nx_irq_wake_t *wake, const nx_irq_policy_t *policy, const nx_irq_source_t *source)¶

Validate actual IRQ facts against an explicit kernel policy.

Note

Cold check without attachment or callback effects. No kernel target is accepted by NONE. PRIMASK permits every valid configurable IRQ with its fixed zero priority group. Kernel-calling BASEPRI targets require the maintained preemption grouping and a numerical priority at least the ceiling. Nonkernel hints do not impose kernel grouping. Binding does not authorize future CPU-context violations.

Parameters:

  • wake – [in] Optional immutable target; NULL disables notification.

  • policy – [in] Immutable validated CPU and kernel configuration.

  • source – [in] External IRQ number, unshifted priority and group.

Returns:

Success, INVALID for malformed facts/target, PERMISSION for a kernel-calling target in an unsafe interrupt domain.

Deliver one bounded hint after authoritative state is latched.

Note

nx_result_t nx_watchdog_port_enable(const nx_watchdog_port_t *port, uint32_t timeout_us, bool debug_freeze, nx_watchdog_state_t *state)¶

Enable IWDG and report its effect and known timing bounds; activation is irreversible.

Note

Success establishes nominal hardware programming, not a guaranteed deadline. Both timeout bounds remain zero when oscillator limits are unknown. A product requiring bounded timing must admit the oscillator profile before activation. Enable runs in a privileged task and is serialized with feed, state and platform stop. Install IRQ feeding only after this call returns; activation does not support a concurrent reload during shadow-register programming.

Parameters:

  • port – [inout] Fixed provider; product owns feed/recovery policy.

  • timeout_us – [in] Requested nominal timeout in maintained range.

  • debug_freeze – [in] Requested CPU-managed debug-freeze setting; external debugger configuration is outside this request.

  • state – [out] Actual timeout bounds and remaining effect, including enabled=true when later setup reports failure after enabling.

Returns:

Success or INVALID/STATE/UNSUPPORTED/IO; never claims enabled hardware was disabled during rollback. Existing enable is identified. A provider without CPU debug-control access rejects true with UNSUPPORTED before activation; it neither queries nor changes external debugger control.

struct nx_watchdog_state_t¶
#include <watchdog.h>

Hardware-selected timeout bounds, including declared LSI uncertainty.

Note

A zero minimum and maximum mean the timeout bounds are unknown, for example while hardware shadow updates remain pending or no oscillator limits have been reviewed. The enabled and irreversible facts remain valid. debug_freeze reports the provider-supported firmware configuration. Providers with CPU-readable debug control observe its setting. A provider without CPU debug-control access supports false only; that value does not observe or describe an external debugger’s setting.
